c5-k3.instrument: Sales pipeline records and referral records

measurement.counted_event: Count each distinct lead that referral records and sales pipeline records identify as referred, enterprise-relevant, and connected to the partner proof pack or approved referral language before qualification. A referred qualified lead must have observable buyer eligibility for the named audience, topic or intent relevant to The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, attributable referral evidence, and a sales pipeline record showing the lead reached the campaign's qualified-lead status or equivalent qualifying stage used in the source records.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude duplicate lead records, test records, non-referred inbound leads, referrals with no evidenced referral source, records with no sales pipeline match, leads outside the eligible referral-partner or buyer audience, and irrelevant events not tied to the partner proof pack, The Stop Line, Signed by Humans or approved referral language. Do not exclude eligible referred leads for unrelated campaign governance, approval or content-quality failures.

c2-k6.metric: Qualified enterprise leads connected to The Stop Line
c2-k6.instrument: Sales pipeline records and The Stop Line route-attribution records

measurement.counted_event: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed enterprise-lead qualification definition required by the registered source is recorded. Once recorded, count each distinct lead record for a United States or European Union buyer that sales pipeline records confirm meets that agreed qualification definition and route-attribution records connect to The Stop Line before qualification through The Stop Line proof page, Signed by Humans founder content, partner proof pack or approved referral language.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude duplicate records for the same lead, buyers outside the United States or European Union, records that do not meet the recorded agreed enterprise-lead qualification definition, and records with no evidenced The Stop Line campaign touchpoint before qualification. Do not exclude eligible connected leads because they did not book a meeting, close, receive governance approval, appear in reporting, or meet unrelated campaign quality requirements.

c4-k6.metric: Qualified inbound conversations from founder content

measurement.counted_event: Each inbound conversation event in inbound-response records where an external contact from the card audience starts or replies in a conversation connected to approved Signed by Humans founder content by a tracked response, named post reference, tagged click path, reply, direct message, form source or other recorded campaign touchpoint. A conversation qualifies when the record shows observable audience eligibility, topic or intent relevant to Signed by Humans, The Stop Line, proof, senior responsibility, AI-supported delivery, referral, buyer interest or senior Sofia talent interest, and attributable evidence linking it to the founder content. Count the conversation itself; it does not need to become a sales-qualified lead, booked meeting, completed sale or approved follow-up.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude records with no founder-content connection, duplicate records for the same conversation, internal or test responses, spam, irrelevant conversations, contacts outside the card audience, records outside the campaign read period, and conversations lacking observable topic or intent relevance to the named outcome. Do not exclude eligible conversations merely because they are unresolved, not sales-qualified, not approved, not escalated or did not become meetings or leads.

c8-k5.instrument: Inbound-response records and sales pipeline records

measurement.counted_event: Count each distinct completed conversation event in inbound-response records or sales pipeline records where an external technical buyer, including a CTO, architecture owner or comparable technical decision or influence role, discusses The Stop Line technical proof story or approved proof assets. A conversation qualifies when the record shows audience eligibility, topic or intent tied to technical proof of AI-supported delivery, senior ownership, claim limits or proof assets, and attribution to the technical proof story or approved proof assets through a recorded touchpoint, reply, message thread, form source, meeting note or tagged campaign path.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude internal discussions, duplicate records of the same conversation event, enquiries or threads with no evidenced technical-buyer participant, conversations not tied to The Stop Line technical proof story or approved proof assets, irrelevant or spam events, non-technical conversations, later sales stages that are not themselves the named conversation event, and prepared or approved responses that were not sent or published to the recipient.

c9-k4.metric: Qualified inbound conversations after earned exposure
c9-k4.instrument: Inbound-response records and sales pipeline records

measurement.counted_event: One distinct inbound conversation thread recorded in inbound-response records and/or sales pipeline records where an eligible external contact in the card audience, meaning a professional influencer, journalist, analyst, named expert or enterprise buyer reached through credible third parties, sends an inbound enquiry or reply after traceable earned exposure to The Stop Line. For this operational calculation, the thread qualifies when the record shows all of: observable audience eligibility; topic or intent tied to The Stop Line proof, proof-led earned coverage, expert discussion, partner or referral opportunity, or enterprise-buyer interest; attributable earned-exposure evidence before the inbound message; and enough recorded thread evidence to distinguish it from duplicates and irrelevant events. Count the conversation thread, not later lead qualification, booked meetings, sales follow-up, sales-qualified status, coverage publication or reporting completion.
measurement.exclusions: Exclude outbound-only outreach with no inbound enquiry or reply sent by the external contact, prepared or approved responses that were not sent or published to the recipient, spam, vendor solicitations, employee-only chatter, duplicate records of the same thread, inbound messages before the traceable earned exposure, untraceable conversations, and conversations whose recorded topic or intent is not connected to The Stop Line proof or earned validation. Do not exclude otherwise eligible conversations merely because a later governance approval, sales follow-up, booked meeting, completed sale or coverage result did not occur.

judgments.reason: The calculation identifies the exact conflict areas, source population, unresolved status and duplicate/correction exclusions, so the count can be calculated without guessing.
judgments.quote: Each unresolved public-profile conflict area found in the Public-profile audit across founding year, headcount, address, legal name, domain identity or nearshore-price language, counted while the audited public source still carries the conflict without evidenced correction.

judgments.reason: The calculation preserves approval status, proof-type requirements and reference-register traceability, matching the registered proof-asset definition.
judgments.quote: Each distinct approved proof asset in The Stop Line proof library with a recorded approval status and proof type marked as named reference, verifiable anonymous reference, technical artifact or internal demo; reference assets must also be traceable in the client-approved reference register.

judgments.reason: The denominator keeps all public AI claims in scope and the numerator requires proof, owner, limit, technical confirmation and final sign-off before release.
judgments.quote: Denominator claims that, before being sent or published, show approved proof, a senior owner, the stop line or stated limit, recorded claim-level and AI-language technical confirmation, and final sign-off for positioning, proof lane, claims and public references.

judgments.reason: The event, page, analytics source and traffic exclusions are concrete enough to count proof-page visits without excluding non-engaged eligible visits.
judgments.quote: One website-analytics visit/session in which a visitor views The Stop Line proof page, with campaign tagging read from the required UTM fields where present.

judgments.reason: This is an instrument-defined analytics duration with clear page-load start, analytics end conditions and relevant exclusions, so open-case waiting rules are not needed.
judgments.quote: The visitor leaves The Stop Line proof page, closes the session, becomes inactive according to the analytics session-timeout rule, or navigates to another page or tracked action.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts a tracked proof-item inspection on the proof page and separates invalid events from eligible repeat opens.
judgments.quote: One tracked proof-item open on The Stop Line proof page, where a visitor expands, opens or otherwise inspects the proof behind an approved claim before any meeting request or AI-story acceptance step.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures clicks to a qualified-meeting route, not later meeting approval or conversion, which matches the click outcome.
judgments.quote: Exclude internal team traffic, bot/spam traffic, test clicks, broken clicks not sent to the recipient system, and clicks not tied to a qualified-meeting route. Do not exclude eligible clicks because the meeting is not later approved, booked or converted to a lead.

judgments.reason: The denominator includes eligible public AI claims and the numerator requires approved proof, senior owner and stated limit before release.
judgments.quote: Eligible public AI claims that, before release, show approved proof, a senior owner and the stop line or stated limit in the claim approval register and public-release checklist.

judgments.reason: The item correctly makes the aggregate unavailable until the agreed enterprise-lead qualification definition required by the source is recorded.
judgments.quote: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed enterprise-lead qualification definition required by the registered source is recorded. Once recorded, count each distinct lead record for a United States or European Union buyer that sales pipeline records confirm meets that agreed qualification definition and route-attribution records connect to The Stop Line before qualification through The Stop Line proof page, Signed by Humans founder content, partner proof pack or approved referral language.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines engaged visits through configured analytics engagement events tied to the proof page and handles duplicate hits separately.
judgments.quote: One website analytics visit/session to The Stop Line proof page during the measurement period that records at least one configured proof-page engagement event, such as an analytics engaged-session event for that page, a proof-item open, or a qualified meeting click from that page.

judgments.reason: The denominator requires exposure to both tested messages and the numerator captures preference for the control-led message, so the split is calculable.
judgments.quote: Sampled owners of midsize businesses in the Owner message test who were exposed to both the control-led message and the artificial-intelligence-capability alternative, both anchored in The Stop Line, and had an opportunity to record one message preference.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the owner sample, exposure, answer opportunity and correct-answer criteria for the comprehension measure.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator whose answer correctly explains that The Stop Line gives more control and visibility by showing approved proof, senior responsibility and the limit the system will not cross, without requiring the owner to become a technical buyer.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures trust movement using matched pre- and post-exposure readings and keeps flat or negative movement in the denominator.
judgments.quote: Exclude non-owner respondents, duplicate respondent records, test or staff records, records outside the test wave, records without verified message exposure, and records missing either the pre-exposure or post-exposure trust reading; do not exclude flat or negative trust movement.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the exposed owner population and positive post-exposure meeting-intent numerator without requiring a later meeting.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator who indicate positive intent after message exposure to take, request or accept a next meeting about The Stop Line or The B Team.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts coded reason themes tied to valid message choices and excludes only invalid or uncodable records.
judgments.quote: Each coded theme occurrence recorded in the Owner message-test reason register from a respondent's submitted reason for choosing either tested message, tied to that respondent's valid message choice.

judgments.reason: The calculation ties reactions to approved Signed by Humans founder launch content, platform analytics and the campaign read period.
judgments.quote: Reactions recorded by LinkedIn analytics or Substack analytics on approved Signed by Humans founder content published for the Month 5 founder launch post, counted by founder and post during the campaign read period.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts comments on approved founder launch content and does not exclude negative or low-quality eligible comments.
judgments.quote: Exclude comments on unapproved content, non-founder content, content outside the Signed by Humans founder launch activity, duplicate analytics records, and comments not attributable to the measured post. Do not exclude negative, neutral, unanswered or low-quality eligible comments unless the analytics source identifies them as spam or platform-invalid.

judgments.reason: The calculation handles shares and saves only where the platform reports them and prevents unavailable saves from being treated as zero.
judgments.quote: Exclude unavailable metrics, unapproved content, non-founder content, content outside the Signed by Humans founder launch activity, duplicate analytics records, and shares or saves not attributable to the measured post. Do not treat unavailable saves as zero unless the source reports zero.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts proof-page clicks attributable to approved founder content through required campaign tags.
judgments.quote: Clicks from approved Signed by Humans founder content to the owned proof page, recorded in the website analytics report through the required campaign tags for the founder content route.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines partner reshares, the eligible content set, the register and the launch read period.
judgments.quote: Partner reshares of the approved Signed by Humans founder launch content or social-pack content, recorded in the social-pack reshare register during the Month 5 launch read period.

judgments.reason: The calculation gives source-consistent operational criteria for qualified inbound conversations and correctly avoids requiring sales qualification or meetings.
judgments.quote: Each inbound conversation event in inbound-response records where an external contact from the card audience starts or replies in a conversation connected to approved Signed by Humans founder content by a tracked response, named post reference, tagged click path, reply, direct message, form source or other recorded campaign touchpoint. A conversation qualifies when the record shows observable audience eligibility, topic or intent relevant to Signed by Humans, The Stop Line, proof, senior responsibility, AI-supported delivery, referral, buyer interest or senior Sofia talent interest, and attributable evidence linking it to the founder content. Count the conversation itself; it does not need to become a sales-qualified lead, booked meeting, completed sale or approved follow-up.

judgments.reason: The calculation uses platform-reported unique reach or equivalent account-level fields rather than engagement actions or impressions alone.
judgments.quote: Unique recipient accounts shown or delivered the published Month 5 Signed by Humans founder launch post in LinkedIn analytics or Substack analytics during the measurement period, using platform-reported reach, unique viewers, unique recipients or equivalent account-level audience reached fields rather than reactions, comments, shares, saves, clicks or inbound replies.

judgments.reason: The proposed scoring rubric has observable eligible events, a defined scale and anchors that measure founder-post engagement quality.
judgments.quote: Score each eligible engagement event on the founder launch post using the engagement-quality rubric: 0 points for passive or unclear engagement such as a reaction, save or unqualified click with no evident relevance; 1 point for a relevant proof-page click, share or comment showing basic attention to Signed by Humans, The Stop Line, proof or senior ownership; 2 points for an engaged comment, reshare or inbound conversation that reflects understanding of senior responsibility, approved proof or the stop line; 3 points for qualified buyer, partner or senior-talent engagement that asks a substantive question, repeats the proof-led message accurately, or creates a credible follow-up conversation. Eligible events include LinkedIn and Substack reactions, comments, shares, saves where available, proof-page clicks and qualified inbound conversations attributable to the founder launch post.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts successful tagged downloads of the partner pack and excludes views, retries and non-pack assets.
judgments.quote: A successful tagged analytics download event for the partner proof pack asset during the measurement period.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only delivered partner briefings recorded through required partner-proof content, excluding planned or incomplete sessions.
judgments.quote: A partner briefing for referral or ecosystem partners that is recorded in the completion register as delivered through its required partner-proof content.

judgments.reason: The calculation provides operational criteria for referred qualified leads using buyer eligibility, referral evidence, source relevance and pipeline qualification status.
judgments.quote: Count each distinct lead that referral records and sales pipeline records identify as referred, enterprise-relevant, and connected to the partner proof pack or approved referral language before qualification. A referred qualified lead must have observable buyer eligibility for the named audience, topic or intent relevant to The Stop Line or Signed by Humans, attributable referral evidence, and a sales pipeline record showing the lead reached the campaign's qualified-lead status or equivalent qualifying stage used in the source records.

judgments.reason: The percentage keeps all required partner-language AI claim checks in the denominator and counts only evidenced compliant checks in the numerator.
judgments.quote: All partner-language AI claim checks required for partner pack, briefing, release or referral language sent or published to partners during the measurement period.

judgments.reason: The calculation does not define how the operator identifies or verifies that an engagement is by or attributable to senior Sofia talent, so qualifying observations require guessing.
judgments.quote: Each LinkedIn or Substack engagement action during the monthly Month 6-Month 12 reporting window on approved Signed by Humans senior craft story content by, or attributable to, the senior Sofia talent audience; qualifying actions include platform-recorded reactions, comments, shares, saves where available, newsletter clicks, replies or other recorded engagement actions tied to the craft story asset.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts LinkedIn profile visits only when analytics attributes them to a defined talent route, campaign tag or referral path.
judgments.quote: Each LinkedIn profile visit recorded during the monthly reporting window that is attributable in the LinkedIn analytics report to a senior-talent route, such as the senior craft story series, talent-facing post route, campaign tag or referral path.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines senior Sofia candidate interest by person, geography, role level, interest evidence and campaign-asset tie.
judgments.quote: Each distinct person from the Sofia senior-engineering talent audience who shows candidate interest through an application, referral, direct inbound message or recruitment-review record, and whose record evidences both senior-engineering qualification and a tie to approved The Stop Line or Signed by Humans story assets.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines eligible buyer engagement actions and correctly counts sent or published responses rather than prepared responses.
judgments.quote: Each buyer engagement action during the monthly reporting window tied to craft-linked proof, including an engaged proof-page visit, proof-item open, qualified meeting click, or inbound buyer response connected to a Signed by Humans craft story, The Stop Line proof page, approved proof item or tagged campaign path. A response qualifies when the message or form submission is sent or published to its recipient, not when prepared or approved.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts tagged proof-page clicks from craft stories and excludes traffic without observable craft-story attribution.
judgments.quote: Each website analytics click event from a Signed by Humans senior craft story to The Stop Line proof page or a proof-page item, identified by campaign tags, UTM fields or equivalent source-path evidence for the craft story asset.

judgments.reason: The duration rule states the reporting cutoff, completed-response cohort, completed count, unavailable result when none complete, and separate open-case aging.
judgments.quote: For each reporting read, use the stated reporting cutoff timestamp and calculate mean hours only for eligible conversation items whose first response was sent or published to the recipient by that cutoff; report the completed-response count used. Escalation, preparation, approval, routing, administrative handoff or the reporting cutoff itself does not stop the clock. If no eligible items have a completed response by the cutoff, report the mean as unavailable.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts distinct issues resolved with evidence through approved answer routes while keeping unresolved eligible issues in the register outside the resolved count.
judgments.quote: Exclude duplicate records for the same issue, non-eligible administrative items, and items outside Month 6 through Month 12. Do not exclude unresolved, unsuccessfully handled, escalated or late eligible issues from the register; they simply do not count as resolved.

judgments.reason: The denominator includes all sent or published eligible responses, and the numerator defines consistency against the approved answer set and do-not-say boundary.
judgments.quote: Eligible denominator messages that match the approved answer set: proof comes before promotion, any AI claim stays linked to approved proof, senior ownership and stated limits, and no do-not-say or widened AI promise appears.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts sent or published reuse of approved answers with a recorded approved-answer source and excludes drafts or unapproved custom answers.
judgments.quote: Each sent or published eligible response or newsroom message that reuses an approved answer from the approved answer set, Q&A/FAQ or Key-Message Table, with the approved answer source recorded in the reuse register.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts recorded senior escalations triggered by the listed crisis tripwires and does not count missed or unresolved issues as escalations.
judgments.quote: Each recorded escalation sent to a senior person before publication because an eligible issue triggered a litigation, disclosure, deal, restructuring, life-safety or regulatory crisis tripwire.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines the sampled technical-buyer population, proof-stimulus exposure and trust-response numerator tied to taking a next meeting.
judgments.quote: Respondents in the denominator who say The Stop Line gives enough evidence to take a next meeting.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts website views of technical proof-story artifacts and excludes non-technical, untagged and duplicate instrumentation events.
judgments.quote: Website analytics events recording a view of technical proof-story artifact content under The Stop Line, including technical artifacts, architecture notes, approved demos, proof labels or related technical proof assets.

judgments.reason: This is an instrument-defined analytics duration with campaign-tagged start and analytics engaged-time endpoint rules.
judgments.quote: The visitor exits, closes, navigates away from or becomes inactive on the tagged technical proof content session according to the analytics tool's engaged-time rule.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts buyer-facing sales uses of the technical proof story and excludes internal preparation or unsent approvals.
judgments.quote: A recorded sales use of the technical proof story in a buyer-facing sales context, such as sending, presenting or publishing the story to a prospect or using it in a qualified sales conversation.

judgments.reason: The calculation gives observable criteria for qualified technical conversations and excludes later sales stages that are not the named conversation event.
judgments.quote: Exclude internal discussions, duplicate records of the same conversation event, enquiries or threads with no evidenced technical-buyer participant, conversations not tied to The Stop Line technical proof story or approved proof assets, irrelevant or spam events, non-technical conversations, later sales stages that are not themselves the named conversation event, and prepared or approved responses that were not sent or published to the recipient.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts confirmed earned briefings with eligible third-party recipients and excludes unconfirmed invitations and paid placements.
judgments.quote: An earned outreach briefing secured in Month 10: a proof-led briefing about The Stop Line with a journalist, analyst, named expert, professional influencer or credible third-party route, recorded after the eligible recipient or representative confirms the briefing or accepts the briefing invitation.

judgments.reason: The calculation preserves the source-listed quality criteria and correctly makes the aggregate unavailable until the agreed threshold is recorded.
judgments.quote: Aggregate unavailable until the agreed quality threshold is recorded in the registered sources. Score each denominator item against the source-listed criteria: priority outlet/influencer, priority-audience relevance, key-message inclusion, positive or neutral tone, brand/spokesperson prominence, desired call to action and original reporting vs syndication; once the agreed threshold exists, count items meeting it.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines proof citations by distinct cited proof source or proof type in eligible earned coverage and excludes generic mentions without proof components.
judgments.quote: A proof citation in earned coverage: one recorded instance in an eligible published earned coverage item where the coverage explicitly cites, links to, quotes or names an approved The Stop Line proof source or proof type, including the proof page, proof library asset, named reference, verifiable anonymous reference, technical artifact, internal demo, senior owner or stated limit. Count one citation per coverage item per distinct cited proof source or proof type.

judgments.reason: The calculation proposes observable source-consistent criteria for qualified inbound conversations after earned exposure without requiring later lead or meeting outcomes.
judgments.quote: One distinct inbound conversation thread recorded in inbound-response records and/or sales pipeline records where an eligible external contact in the card audience, meaning a professional influencer, journalist, analyst, named expert or enterprise buyer reached through credible third parties, sends an inbound enquiry or reply after traceable earned exposure to The Stop Line. For this operational calculation, the thread qualifies when the record shows all of: observable audience eligibility; topic or intent tied to The Stop Line proof, proof-led earned coverage, expert discussion, partner or referral opportunity, or enterprise-buyer interest; attributable earned-exposure evidence before the inbound message; and enough recorded thread evidence to distinguish it from duplicates and irrelevant events. Count the conversation thread, not later lead qualification, booked meetings, sales follow-up, sales-qualified status, coverage publication or reporting completion.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts distinct registered advocates only after they send or publish an advocacy post or share, excluding training without action.
judgments.quote: Each registered employee advocate or approved supporter advocate who, after Conversation Management training, sends or publishes at least one Month 11 Signed by Humans advocacy post or share using the provided language or proof link.

judgments.reason: The calculation defines post-quality compliance by approved language, proof links, proof boundary, do-not-say lines and escalation routing.
judgments.quote: Published denominator posts that stay inside approved Signed by Humans language, include approved proof links where the post makes a claim, preserve the proof boundary and do-not-say lines, and route questions the advocate should not answer themselves to escalation rather than inventing claims.

judgments.reason: The metric promises engagement quality, but the calculation only counts relevant non-spam engagement actions without a quality scale, anchors or score meaning.
judgments.quote: Each relevant, non-spam engagement action on a Month 11 advocate post recorded in LinkedIn analytics or inbound-response records, including reactions, substantive comments, reposts or shares, saves where available, proof-page click-throughs, and qualified inbound responses tied to the post.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts tagged proof-page clicks from Month 11 advocate posts and excludes unattributable or duplicate traffic.
judgments.quote: Each website analytics click event landing on the approved proof page from a Month 11 advocate post with the required campaign identifier or UTM tags for the employee advocacy push.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts logged escalations from advocate questions that use the Conversation Management route for defined proof, claim, technical, legal or approval issues.
judgments.quote: Each logged escalation from an advocate question in the Month 11 employee advocacy push where the advocate uses the Conversation Management route for a proof, claim, do-not-say, technical, legal, disclosure, crisis-tripwire, or approval question they should not answer themselves.

judgments.reason: The calculation measures completion of the Month 12 executive scorecard within the ten-working-day reporting window stated by the source.
judgments.quote: Executive scorecard completion recorded when the Month 12 one-page after-campaign executive scorecard is produced within ten working days of the final campaign reading.

judgments.reason: The denominator includes all headline KPIs on the scorecard and the numerator requires baseline, target, result and trend fields for each.
judgments.quote: Headline KPIs on the scorecard that each report baseline, target, result and trend in readable fields.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts only approved Key-Message Table changes after measurement review with evidence, review date and approval record.
judgments.quote: Key-Message Table message change approved after the measurement review, where the register shows the changed message, supporting evidence or proof gap, review date and approval record.

judgments.reason: The calculation requires each next-year proof gap to name the missing proof, affected claim or message and Month 12 evidence establishing the gap.
judgments.quote: Next-year proof gap named in the proof-gap register, with the missing proof, affected claim or message, and the evidence from Month 12 measurement that establishes the gap.

judgments.reason: The calculation counts completion only when the quarter-end evaluation narrative addresses enterprise-lead contribution using quarter-end evidence.
judgments.quote: Quarter-end enterprise-lead contribution review completed when the quarter-end evaluation narrative records whether The Stop Line and Signed by Humans contributed to the enterprise-lead target using the quarter-end review evidence.
